body.translated_text: Oṃ, homage to the Three Jewels!

children.text: pūrvāvadānacariteṣu suduṣkareṣu gīteṣu yasya surakiṃnarasundarībhiḥ |
children.translated_text: He whose former <s>avadāna</s> (heroic deed) narratives, most difficult to perform, are sung by <s>sura</s> (divine), <s>kiṃnara</s>, and celestial maidens —

children.text: adyāpi candrakiraṇairiva saṃkucanti mārāṅganāvadanapaṅkajakānanāni || Śl_1 ||
children.translated_text: even now, as if by moonbeams, the lotus-faces of <s>Māra's</s> women shrink and wilt. (Verse 1)

children.text: saubhāgyahṛdyavapuṣaḥ paramādbhutasya yasyālpapuṇyajanadurlabhadarśanasya |
children.translated_text: Of him whose form is charming in its auspicious beauty, supremely wondrous, whose sight is unattainable by those of little merit —

children.text: saṃpāditābhimatalokamanorathasya cintāmaṇeriva parārtharasaikavṛttiḥ || Śl_2 ||
children.translated_text: like a wish-fulfilling gem, his sole activity is devotion to the welfare of others, who has fulfilled the heart's desires of all beings. (Verse 2)

children.text: yaḥ sarvadā parasukhaikaraso babhūva duḥkhena duḥkhamagamatparamaṃ pareṣām |
children.translated_text: He who was always solely devoted to the happiness of others, who suffered the utmost suffering at the suffering of others —

children.text: atyarthamāhitamahākaruṇāguṇasya yasyātmaduḥkhasukhamantaritaṃ tadeva || Śl_3 ||
children.translated_text: for him, endowed with the great quality of infinite compassion, his own suffering and happiness were eclipsed by that very [compassion for others]. (Verse 3)

children.text: vicchi x māvayasi yasya śiraḥ parārtha x x x sannayanapaṅkajatāmavāpa |
children.translated_text: He who... you sever his head for the sake of others... attained the state of a lotus-eyed one —

children.text: svārthaṃ puna x x x x x sitātapatrā pṛthvī babhūva niśiteva kṛpāṇadhārā || Śl_4 ||
children.translated_text: but for his own sake... the earth with its white parasol became like the edge of a sharp sword. (Verse 4)

children.text: lokopakāranirataprakaṭodayena śulka x x x x x x guṇojjvalena |
children.translated_text: By him, whose rising is manifest, devoted to the welfare of the world, resplendent with... virtues —

children.text: doṣāndhakārabhidureṇa manorameṇa yenoditena śaśineva jagatprakāśam || Śl_5 ||
children.translated_text: the destroyer of the darkness of faults, delightful — by his rising, the world is illuminated as if by the moon. (Verse 5)

children.text: cūḍāvibhūṣaṇamivottamaratnakalpamūḍhaṃ śirobhirurubhiḥ phaṇināṃ x x x |
children.translated_text: Like a crest-jewel comparable to the finest gem, borne upon the heads and thighs of the serpent kings...,

children.text: yacchāsanaṃ śubhamakhaṇḍaviśuddhavṛttaṃ pātālamūrdhani layatimiraṃ pramārṣṭi || Śl_6 ||
children.translated_text: his auspicious teaching, of unblemished pure conduct, dispels the darkness of delusion even in the depths of the netherworld. (Verse 6)

children.text: dharmāmbuvāha iva yo 'bhyudito hitāya dharmāmṛtaṃ jalamivaikarasaṃ vavarṣa |
children.translated_text: He who arose like a <s>dharma</s>-rain-cloud for the benefit of all, rained down the nectar of <s>Dharma</s> like water of a single essence —

children.text: tāpāpa x x x x x x x x x x x x yadanekarasa x x x x x x x x x x x x x x || Śl_7 ||
children.translated_text: removing the heat... of various essences... (Verse 7)

children.text: vistīrṇanimnavimalaprakaṭāśrayeṣu pātreṣu sarvaparimardasaheṣu yeṣu |
children.translated_text: In vessels that are broad, deep, pure, and openly receptive, capable of withstanding all handling —

children.text: tatsaṃsthitaṃ bhavati sarvajanopakāraṃ x x x x x x x x x x x x x x || Śl_8 ||
children.translated_text: that which is placed therein becomes beneficial for all people... (Verse 8)

children.text: tajjāgaraṃ maraṇajanmajarāpahāri ye nāpnuvanti na pibanti na dhārayanti |
children.translated_text: That wakefulness which removes death, birth, and old age — those who do not attain it, do not drink it, do not preserve it —

children.text: te māhitā bahulamohamahāmadena x x x x x x x x x dhamādriyante || Śl_9 ||
children.translated_text: they, intoxicated by the great madness of abundant delusion,... do not regard it. (Verse 9)

children.text: cakṣuryadekamamalaṃ jagato 'khilasya sādhāraṇaṃ tribhuvanasya yadekadīpaḥ |
children.translated_text: That which is the one pure eye of the entire world, that which is the one lamp common to the three realms —

children.text: tacchāsanaṃ samadhigamya yadutsṛjanti mohasya tadvilasitaṃ paramādbhutasya || Śl_10 ||
children.translated_text: having attained that teaching, those who then abandon it — that is the play of supreme, wondrous delusion. (Verse 10)

children.text: śikṣā x x x viditeṣviva bodhisaudhasopānapaddhatipadeṣu padaṃ dadhānāḥ |
children.translated_text: Those who place their feet upon the training... like steps on the stairway leading to the palace of <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) —

children.text: tuṅgāṃ prayānti padavīmanivartamānā bhūmiṃ nijāmavataranti vivartamānāḥ || Śl_11 ||
children.translated_text: ascend to the lofty path without turning back, but descend to their own level when they do turn back. (Verse 11)

children.text: janmārṇavaṃ paramadustaramuttitīrṣuḥ śīlaplavaṃ ka iha hastagataṃ jahāti |
children.translated_text: Who, wishing to cross the ocean of birth, which is supremely difficult to cross, would abandon the raft of <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct) once it is in hand?

children.text: kāntāramadhyapatitaḥ kathamāryasārthādbhraṣṭo na śocati ciraṃ supathānabhijñaḥ || Śl_12 ||
children.translated_text: How can one who has fallen in the middle of a wilderness, separated from the noble caravan, not grieve for a long time, being ignorant of the good path? (Verse 12)

children.text: saṃsārabhūdharadarījaṭharaprapātādutthātumudyataparāḥ paramāndhakārāt |
children.translated_text: Those striving to rise from the abyss of the cave-belly of the mountain of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence), from the utter darkness,

children.text: muñcanti ye jinaguṇāvalimantarāle vegena te viṣamapātamadhaḥ patanti || Śl_13 ||
children.translated_text: who let go of the chain of the <s>Jina's</s> (Victor's) virtues midway — they fall downward with speed into the precipice. (Verse 13)

children.text: ekākino 'pi manasā niyamaṃ prakalpya ye karmaṇā samuditena samunnayanti |
children.translated_text: Those who, even while alone, having resolved a discipline in their minds, uplift themselves through accumulated <s>karma</s> (action) —

children.text: te sādhavo bhuvanamaṇḍalamaulibhūtāstaireva yānti gurutāṃ guravaḥ suśiṣyaiḥ || Śl_14 ||
children.translated_text: those noble ones become the crest-jewels of the circle of the world; by such excellent disciples, teachers attain their greatness. (Verse 14)

children.text: labdhvā guṇaughajananīṃ jananīmivāryāmatyantaśuddahṛdayāmanuvartamānāḥ |
children.translated_text: Having found a noble mother who is the source of a flood of virtues, like one's own mother, of utterly pure heart, following her —

children.text: tejasvinaḥ sukhamasūnapi saṃtyajanti satyasthitivyasanino na punaḥ pratijñām || Śl_15 ||
children.translated_text: the brilliant ones easily abandon even their lives, but never their vow, being devoted to steadfastness in truth. (Verse 15)

children.text: tiṣṭhantu tāvadiha sarvajanāpavādāḥ sarvāśca pāpagatayo nirayāśca ghorāḥ |
children.translated_text: Let alone all the censure of people in this world, and all the evil destinies and terrible hells —

children.text: sadyo jahāti sahajāṃ prakṛtiṃ yadeṣa duḥkhaṃ tataḥ kimaparaṃ bhuvi sajjanasya || Śl_16 ||
children.translated_text: if one immediately abandons one's innate nature, what greater suffering is there for a good person on earth? (Verse 16)

children.text: yaḥ prapya nāvamiva dharmamayīṃ viśālāṃ bhūyo jahāti padavīṃ munibhiḥ praklṛptām |
children.translated_text: He who, having obtained the vast ship of <s>Dharma</s>, again abandons the path established by the sages —

children.text: saṃsārasāgaravivartananartaneṣu cetaḥspṛhā taralitā niyamena tasya || Śl_17 ||
children.translated_text: in the dances of whirling through the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>, his mind's desire is inevitably made restless. (Verse 17)

children.text: saṃsāracakramaniśaṃ parivartamānamāruhya yaḥ sukhamavaiti vivartamānaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who, having mounted the ever-revolving wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s>, finds comfort while it turns —

children.text: so 'vaśyameva tarivaśaṃ masaḥ krameṇa sarvāḥ samāśca visamāśca gatīḥ prayāti || Śl_18 ||
children.translated_text: he inevitably, gradually falling under its power, traverses all the even and uneven destinies. (Verse 18)

children.text: atyugragandhamaśuciprakaroparuddhamatyantasaṃkaṭamupoḍhaghanāndhakāram |
children.translated_text: Extremely foul-smelling, obstructed by impure masses, exceedingly narrow, filled with dense darkness —

children.text: āviśya garbhanilayaṃ nirayaṃ yathaiva duḥkhaṃ mahatsa sahate paripiṇḍatāṅgaḥ || Śl_19 ||
children.translated_text: entering the abode of the womb as if it were a hell, he endures great suffering, with his limbs compressed into a ball. (Verse 19)

children.text: kālakramena sa tato dṛḍhatailayantraniṣpīḍyamāna iva yāti bhuvaṃ kathaṃcit |
children.translated_text: In the course of time, as if being squeezed through a tight oil-press, he somehow comes forth into the world —

children.text: sadyastathāpi yadayaṃ na jahāti jīvaṃ duḥkhopabhogagatidurlabhi tattadeva || Śl_20 ||
children.translated_text: yet even then he does not immediately abandon life — that itself is the difficulty of attaining the path of experiencing suffering. (Verse 20)

children.text: tatra sthitaṃ tamaśucau parivartamānamārdrolbaveṣṭitatanuṃ bahalogragandham |
children.translated_text: Remaining there in that impure state, turning about, wrapped in the moist membrane, his body intensely foul-smelling —

children.text: pūrvasmṛtivraṇamivolbaṇadoṣapākaṃ bhinnaṃ jahāti ghṛṇayeva nipīḍyamānaḥ || Śl_21 ||
children.translated_text: like a wound of former memory, with the ripening of terrible faults, he is pierced and abandoned with disgust. (Verse 21)

children.text: sarvopacāravivaśaṃ śithilākulāṅgamutsṛjya bālyamupajātakaṇairabhāvaḥ |
children.translated_text: Casting off childhood with its helplessness over all care, with limbs weak and confused, with emerging restlessness —

children.text: tuṅgeṣu yauvanagirīndradarītaṭeṣu mohāyate viṣayadṛṣṭiviṣālayeṣu || Śl_22 ||
children.translated_text: on the lofty mountain-cave slopes of youth, he is deluded in the snake-pits of sensory perception. (Verse 22)

children.text: sa tato'pi patatyacetanaḥ patito naiva jahāti vikriyām |
children.translated_text: From there too he falls, senseless; having fallen, he does not abandon his perversity;

children.text: ajarāmaramātmavigrahaṃ lalitaṃ manyata evaṃ bāliśaḥ || Śl_23 ||
children.translated_text: the fool considers his own body to be free from old age and death, and charming. (Verse 23)

children.text: sa vihāya munīndrasevitaṃ supathaṃ yātyapathena mohitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Having abandoned the good path frequented by the lord of sages, he goes astray on the wrong path, deluded,

children.text: rabhasena parāṃ vicūrṇayan gajavajjātamado niraṅkuśaḥ || Śl_24 ||
children.translated_text: impetuously crushing others, like a maddened elephant without a goad. (Verse 24)

children.text: atha tasya balādanicchataḥ śirasi nyastapadā sunirdayam |
children.translated_text: Then, forcibly, upon the head of that unwilling one, mercilessly placing her foot,

children.text: niśitaṃ palitāṅkuśaṃ jarā kariṇo hastipakīva yacchati || Śl_25 ||
children.translated_text: old age extends the sharp goad of grey hair, like an elephant-driver to an elephant. (Verse 25)

children.text: sa tathāpi vijihyaceṣṭitaḥ kuśalenāpi bhayādivojjhitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Yet even then he remains motionless in conduct, abandoned even by fear and other [warnings], though [prompted] by good deeds;

children.text: sukṛtāni karoti mohitaḥ śaravatsvātmavadhāya puṣpitaḥ || Śl_26 ||
children.translated_text: deluded, he performs meritorious acts that blossom into arrows for his own destruction. (Verse 26)

children.text: atha taṃ prahasannivāntakaḥ palitaughairdarśanairivolbaṇaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Antaka</s> (Death), as if laughing, with floods of grey hair, with terrible appearances,

children.text: śirasi grasituṃ pravartate nirupāyapraśamo jarārujaḥ || Śl_27 ||
children.translated_text: begins to devour him from the head — the disease of old age, whose pacification is beyond remedy. (Verse 27)

children.text: vidalanti tato 'sya sanvayo matirutkrāmati hīyate gatiḥ |
children.translated_text: Then his relatives disperse, his intellect wanders, his gait falters,

children.text: kṣayameti vapuḥ pariślaṣaṃ niyataṃ vardhata eva jīvitāśā || Śl_28 ||
children.translated_text: his body wastes away, emaciated — yet his desire for life only ever increases. (Verse 28)

children.text: kramaśaśca nimīlitendriyo hataśaktirviṣayeṣu lālasaḥ |
children.translated_text: And gradually, with senses closing down, his powers destroyed, still craving for sense-objects,

children.text: upagacchati yāmayaṃ daśāṃ narake sā yadi bhīma eva saḥ || Śl_29 ||
children.translated_text: he approaches the state controlled by <s>Yama</s> (Death) — if that [state] is terrifying, then so indeed is he. (Verse 29)

children.text: kathamevamidaṃ mayā kṛtaṃ kathamevaṃ na kṛtaṃ hatā gatiḥ |
children.translated_text: 'How did I do this? How did I not do that? My destiny is ruined!

children.text: kathamevamayaṃ mayāstakaḥ śirasi nyastapado na lakṣitaḥ || Śl_30 ||
children.translated_text: How was this [death], having placed its foot upon my head, not perceived by me?' (Verse 30)

children.text: iti x x x cittamādhibhiḥ kukṛtaiḥ śokamayairupadrutaḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus... the mind tormented by afflictions and evil deeds that bring sorrow,

children.text: vyadhitena savāṣpavāriṇā karuṇaṃ bandhujanena vīkṣitaḥ || Śl_31 ||
children.translated_text: is looked upon pitifully by relatives with tear-filled [eyes], the body diseased. (Verse 31)

children.text: vinipīḍitamarmabandhanastimiraṃ ghorataraṃ viśanniva |
children.translated_text: With vital connections crushed, entering into a darkness more terrible still,

children.text: vijahāti nijaṃ kaḍevaraṃ dayitaṃ yatnapareṇa rakṣitam || Śl_32 ||
children.translated_text: he abandons his own body, beloved and guarded with great effort. (Verse 32)

children.text: sa virauti gṛhītamūrdhajo yamadūtairdṛḍhapāśasaṃyataḥ |
children.translated_text: He screams, seized by the hair by <s>Yama's</s> messengers, bound with strong nooses —

children.text: na śṛṇoti jano 'sya bhāṣitaṃ svakṛtākrandaravādivākulaḥ || Śl_33 ||
children.translated_text: no one hears his words, bewildered by the sound of their own screaming and wailing. (Verse 33)

children.text: prastāraśailasaridantaradurgameṣu mārgeṣu tīkṣṇatarakaṇṭakasaṃkaṭeṣu |
children.translated_text: On paths impassable through expanses of rocks, mountains, and river-gaps, dense with extremely sharp thorns,

children.text: ghoraiḥ kṛtāntapuruṣairyamadaṇḍaghātamākṛṣyate galaniṣevitakālapāśaḥ || Śl_34 ||
children.translated_text: he is dragged by the terrible servants of <s>Kṛtānta</s> (Death), struck by <s>Yama's</s> staff, with the noose of death fastened around his neck. (Verse 34)

children.text: dūrānnirīkṣya vimalaṃ salilaṃ pipāsurabhyeti gāḍhatṛṣito yadayaṃ tadeva |
children.translated_text: Seeing from afar clear water, this thirsty one approaches it, intensely parched — but that very [water]

children.text: keśaughaśaivalavimiśritapūtipūyapaṅkāpaṅkitaṃ kṣatajavaṃ jalatā prayāti || Śl_35 ||
children.translated_text: mixed with hair-masses and moss, filled with putrid pus and mud, stained with blood, assumes the appearance of water. (Verse 35)

children.text: velānilākulitaśīkaraśītasānumānīlacandanataruṃ malayaṃ prayāti |
children.translated_text: He approaches <s>Malaya</s> mountain, with cool peaks sprayed by wind-stirred waves, with blue sandalwood trees —

children.text: so 'pyasya caṇḍavanadāvaśikhāvalīḍhaśīrṇolmukaprakaradanturatāṃ prayāti || Śl_36 ||
children.translated_text: but even that, for him, assumes the appearance of crumbling firebrands consumed by fierce forest fire-flames. (Verse 36)

children.text: yadyeti vārinidhimudvatabhīmalolakallolabhedajanitolvaṇaphenahāsam |
children.translated_text: If he approaches the ocean, laughing with terrible, huge foam produced by the breaking of towering, fearful, rolling waves —

children.text: so 'pyasya taptaviṣadāruṇasaikatābhravibhrāntakarkaśamarunmarutāṃ prayāti || Śl_37 ||
children.translated_text: even that, for him, assumes the appearance of harsh, blazing winds amid clouds of burning, cruel, terrifying sand. (Verse 37)

children.text: tatra sthitasya jaladāgamaśaṃsino 'sya sāṅgāradhūmakuliśopalavisphuliṅgam |
children.translated_text: For him standing there, who expects the coming of rain-clouds, the rain-cloud rains down

children.text: vidyullatākanakarājipiśaṅgamaṅge nārācavarṣamabhivarṣati vārivahaḥ || Śl_38 ||
children.translated_text: a shower of iron arrows — with embers, smoke, thunderbolts, stones, and sparks — golden-tawny with lightning-creeper flashes upon his body. (Verse 38)

children.text: tāpārditasya dahanaṃ tu hitānilo 'pi śītārditasya dahano 'pi karoti śītam |
children.translated_text: For one tormented by heat, even a beneficial breeze becomes fire; for one tormented by cold, even fire produces cold —

children.text: atyugrakarmapariṇāmavimohitasya viśvaṃ tadāsya viparītamidaṃ vibhāti || Śl_39 ||
children.translated_text: for one deluded by the ripening of extremely terrible <s>karma</s>, everything then appears reversed to him. (Verse 39)

children.text: śūcīmukhasya bahuyojanabhīmakukṣerārtasya vāripibato 'pi mahāsamudre |
children.translated_text: For one with a needle-mouth and a belly terrible for many leagues, even while drinking water in the great ocean, tormented —

children.text: aprāpta eva pṛthukaṇṭhadarīprapātaśleṣmoṣmaṇā jalalavaḥ pariśoṣameti || Śl_40
children.translated_text: even before reaching [the belly], the drop of water is dried up by the heat of phlegm in the wide cavity of the throat. (Verse 40)

children.text: cañcacchaṭānika x pīvarasārameyadaṃṣṭrāṅkurāgrakuliśakṣatacūrṇitāṅgaḥ |
children.translated_text: With body shattered and pulverized by the thunderbolt-sharp tips of the fangs of flashing, stout, excellent hounds...,

children.text: kṣārāmbupūrṇataravaitaraṇītaṭeṣu niṣkṛṣyate viṣamakoṭiśitopaleṣu || Śl_41 ||
children.translated_text: he is dragged out on the banks of the <s>Vaitaraṇī</s> (river of hell), filled with alkaline water, upon jagged sharp-edged stones. (Verse 41)

children.text: dhāvañjavena niśitakṣurasaṃstareṣu vicchinnamūrtirasipattralatāvaneṣu |
children.translated_text: Running swiftly over beds of sharpened razors, his body cut to pieces in the forests of <s>Asipattravana</s> (sword-leaf trees),

children.text: kūpe patatyaśaraṇaḥ śitaśūlaśaktiprāsāsihāsanijitāntakavaktrarandhe || Śl_42 ||
children.translated_text: the shelterless one falls into a pit, into the maw of death's gaping jaws, filled with sharp stakes, spears, javelins, swords, and laughing iron fangs. [Śl 42]

children.text: tīvrātapakvaṣitaduḥsahākhinnadeho vṛkṣānnirīkṣya ghananīladalānupaiti |
children.translated_text: His body unbearably afflicted by fierce, scorching heat, he sees trees with dense dark leaves and approaches them,

children.text: tatpattraśastraśatapātavibhinnamūrtistatraiva tiṣṭhati ciraṃ virutaikabandhuḥ || Śl_43 ||
children.translated_text: but his body is split apart by hundreds of falling leaf-blades, and there he remains for a long time, his only companion being his own screams. [Śl 43]

children.text: paryantanirgataśikhāśatavisphuliṅgamālākulajvalitamaṇḍanamaṇḍitābhiḥ |
children.translated_text: By women adorned with blazing ornaments from whose edges stream hundreds of flame-tips and showers of sparks,

children.text: premāntarapraṇayanirdayamaṅganābhirāliṅgyate krakacakarkaśavigrahābhiḥ || Śl_44 ||
children.translated_text: by those merciless women feigning love and inner affection, whose bodies are rough as saws, he is embraced. [Śl 44]

children.text: śailābhabhīṣaṇavisaṃkaṭameṣayūthasaṃghaṭṭacūrṇitaviśīrṇasamastagātraḥ |
children.translated_text: His entire body crushed and shattered by the collision of fearsome flocks of rams, massive as mountains, pressing together in a narrow defile,

children.text: āpātavātalavaśaityasamarpitāsuḥ saṃcūrṇyate punarasau śataśastathaiva || Śl_45 ||
children.translated_text: his life restored by the cool wind that descends upon him, he is ground to pieces again and again, a hundredfold, in the same way. [Śl 45]

children.text: uttrāsito mukharakhaḍgaśivāsahasrairārohati drutapadaṃ punareva raudrān |
children.translated_text: Terrified by thousands of howling jackals and swords, he swiftly climbs once more the dreadful

children.text: tāṃ kūṭaśālmalimadhomukhakaṇṭhakaughanirbhidyamānavapurarpitagāḍhaśalyaḥ || Śl_46 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kūṭaśālmali</s> (thorny silk-cotton tree), its downward-facing mass of thorns piercing his body, driving deep barbs into him. [Śl 46]

children.text: mṛtyoḥ karāntagalitairiva kālapāśairāśīviṣairdhṛtaphaṇairdṛḍhasaṃyatasya |
children.translated_text: Bound tightly by hooded serpents like the nooses of <s>Kāla</s> (Death), as if slipping from the very hands of <s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death),

children.text: utpāṭayanti nayane sphurataḥ prasahya tatra sthitasya bakavāyasakaṅkagṛdhrāḥ || Śl_47 ||
children.translated_text: herons, crows, cranes, and vultures forcibly tear out the eyes of the one who stands there, still quivering. [Śl 47]

children.text: teṣāṃ mukhaiḥ kuliśakoṭinibhaiḥ prasahya nidrāyamānavapureṣa kṛtārtanādaḥ |
children.translated_text: With their beaks sharp as diamond points, they forcibly torment the one whose body lies helpless, who lets out piteous cries,

children.text: lohonmukhapracurapīvaratīkṣṇaśaṅkunirbhinnamūrtiravarohati naṣṭacetāḥ || Śl_48 ||
children.translated_text: and pierced by the abundant thick sharp iron spikes driven upward, his body shattered, he descends, bereft of consciousness. [Śl 48]

children.text: ādīptaśūlaśitaśalyavibhinnadehāstatraiva kecidavaroḍhumaśaknuvantaḥ |
children.translated_text: Some there, their bodies pierced by blazing stakes and sharp barbs, unable to descend,

children.text: ghorairyadā niśitaśastramukhairayobhirākṛṣyamāṇavisaradgalitāntrasūtrāḥ || Śl_49 ||
children.translated_text: are dragged by terrible iron hooks with sharpened blade-tips, their entrails spilling out loosely as they are pulled apart. [Śl 49]

children.text: kecitpatanti viṣameṣū girestaṭeṣu kecitparikvaṣitatailakaṭāhakukṣau |
children.translated_text: Some fall upon the uneven cliff-faces of mountains; some into cauldrons of boiling oil,

children.text: uttaptavālukabhuvaṃ visṛtasphuliṅgāmenya viśanti padasaṅgamanāpnuvantaḥ || Śl_50 ||
children.translated_text: while others enter grounds of scorching sand showering sparks, unable to gain any foothold. [Śl 50]

children.text: eke punaḥ simisimāyitamūkṣmajantusaṃghātajarjaritasūnavipūtikāyāḥ |
children.translated_text: Still others, their bodies putrid and festering, infested with swarming masses of tiny creatures that gnaw with a hissing sound,

children.text: saṃcālamātramapi hartumaśaknuvanto jīvanti karmamayapāśanibaddhajīvāḥ || Śl_51 ||
children.translated_text: unable even to make the slightest movement to shake them off, they go on living, their life-breaths bound by the fetters of their own <s>karma</s>. [Śl 51]

children.text: asthīnyapi praṇayatā rahitopamena śītena jarjaritavepitapiṇḍitāṅgāḥ |
children.translated_text: Their limbs shivering, trembling, and contracted by a cold beyond all comparison that penetrates even the bones,

children.text: utpannabhinnapiṭakā śatajātajantujagdhakṣataśrutasamajjavaśālaśīkāḥ || Śl_52 ||
children.translated_text: blisters bursting open upon them, their wounds devoured by hundreds of newly born creatures, oozing with pus and marrow. [Śl 52]

children.text: saṃdaṣṭalagnadaśanāstanulomakeśāḥ saṃghaṭṭitavyadhitalocanakarṇakaṇṭhāḥ |
children.translated_text: Their teeth clenched and locked together, their fine body-hair standing on end, their eyes, ears, and throats chafed and wounded by grinding contact,

children.text: ā cetaso jaḍataratvamupetakāyāstiṣṭhanti śītanarakeṣu bhṛśaṃ nadantaḥ || Śl_53 ||
children.translated_text: their bodies reduced to utter numbness down to the mind itself, they remain in the cold hells, crying out violently. [Śl 53]

children.text: vikīrṇabahalogragandhakaṭudhūmadhūmrāntaraṃ vijṛmbhitaśikhākaraprakararudradigmaṇḍalam |
children.translated_text: Its interior darkened by billowing acrid smoke of spreading foul stench, its quarters made terrible by masses of outstretched flame-fingers,

children.text: sitāsthisakalāṭalīracitabhūṣaṇaṃ bhīṣaṇaṃ pravṛttamiva bhairavaṃ sasujacarma hāhāravam || Śl_54 ||
children.translated_text: adorned with ornaments fashioned from heaps of white bone-fragments, terrifying, as if <s>Bhairava</s> himself were performing a dreadful dance with a fresh skin, resounding with cries of 'hāhā!' [Śl 54]

children.text: caṭacchaḍhaditi kvacitsphuradurusphuliṅgākulaṃ chamacchamaditi kṣaṇasthagitajṛmbhitaṃ medasi |
children.translated_text: Here and there crackling 'caṭac-chaḍ' with bursting showers of great sparks, sputtering 'chamac-cham' as flames momentarily subside in the fat,

children.text: kaṭatkaṭaditi kvaṇantamuraso 'sthirandhrāntare patanti narakānalaṃ vijitakalpakālānalam || Śl_55 ||
children.translated_text: the bones rattling 'kaṭat-kaṭ' within the hollows of the chest — they fall into the hell-fire that surpasses the fire at the end of the <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic age). [Śl 55]

children.text: purāṇatṛṇajarjarajvalitaparśukā x x x x x x x x latālavo dhagiti vāntadīptārciṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: Their ribs blazing like old dry grass [...lacuna...] vine-tendrils belching forth blazing flames with a 'dhag!',

children.text: sphuṭajjaṭharaniḥsṛtaprasaradantrasaṃtrāsitāḥ vimuktagurughargharadhvanitamātraśeṣakriyāḥ || Śl_56 ||
children.translated_text: terrified by the entrails streaming out from their burst-open bellies, their only remaining action the utterance of deep gurgling sounds. [Śl 56]

children.text: nirīkṣya vivarāntaraṃ muhurapāvṛtaṃ dūrataḥ prayānti kathamapyamī pramataduḥkhamokṣāśrayāḥ |
children.translated_text: Seeing from afar an opening repeatedly revealed and concealed, these beings somehow make their way toward it, seeking release from their immeasurable suffering,

children.text: yadā tadapi ghaṭṭitaṃ bhavati karmapaṭṭairdṛḍhaistadā viphalavāñchitāḥ kimapi yānti duḥkhāntaram || Śl_57 ||
children.translated_text: but when that opening too is blocked shut by the firm bolts of <s>karma</s>, then, their hopes rendered futile, they pass into yet another realm of suffering. [Śl 57]

children.text: jvalanniśitatomaraprakaravarṣaṇānantaraṃ dravīkṛtamayorasaṃ dahanaraśmimālākulam |
children.translated_text: After a rain of blazing sharp-pointed lances, molten iron liquid, seething with garlands of fiery rays,

children.text: pibanti galadasravo narakapāladaṇḍāhatā mukhaśravaṇanāsikāvivaralabdhadhūmodgamāḥ || Śl_58 ||
children.translated_text: they are forced to drink, struck by the clubs of the hell-wardens, their tears streaming, smoke rising from the openings of their mouths, ears, and nostrils. [Śl 58]

children.text: ādagdhavisphuṭitanetraśiraḥ kapālamastiṣkadīpitapiśaṅgaśikhākalāpaḥ |
children.translated_text: The skull and eye-sockets burnt and split open, crowned with tawny flame-crests blazing from the brain-matter,

children.text: śuṣkendhanaprakaranirdayatāmupaiti śokāgnikoṣa iva gātracayeṣu teṣām || Śl_59 ||
children.translated_text: the fire of grief becomes merciless as a pyre of dry kindling upon those heaps of limbs. [Śl 59]

children.text: te jantavo girinadījalalolajīvā auṣṭhyaṃ tadeva narakeṣu ta eva cāgniḥ |
children.translated_text: Those beings whose lives are tossed about like water in mountain rivers — that very lip-moisture becomes fire in the hells,

children.text: karmāṇi tatkhalu tathā pariṇāmayanti sarvaṃ yathā paramadāruṇamāvibhāti || Śl_60 ||
children.translated_text: for <s>karma</s> indeed ripens in such a way that everything manifests as supremely terrible. [Śl 60]

children.text: ātmīyakarmavivaśākulaveṣṭitasya muktasya pāpanilayānnirayāṃ kathaṃcit |
children.translated_text: For a being helplessly entangled by the force of its own <s>karma</s>, somehow released from the hells, that abode of sin,

children.text: lokeṣvanantagatibhedabhayākuleṣu mānuṣyakaṃ paramadurlabhameva jantoḥ || Śl_61 ||
children.translated_text: human birth is supremely difficult to obtain among the realms beset by fear of countless divisions of rebirth. [Śl 61]

children.text: mleccheṣu vā narakapālasamavrateṣu tiryakṣu vā kṛtaparasparabhakṣaṇeṣu |
children.translated_text: Whether among the <s>mlecchas</s> (barbarians), whose customs resemble those of hell-wardens, or among animals who devour one another,

children.text: jātiṃ labheta yadi tatra tadeva śīlamāsevate patati yena punaḥ prapātam || Śl_62 ||
children.translated_text: if one obtains birth there, one pursues that very same conduct by which one falls again into the abyss. [Śl 62]

children.text: yatprāpya janmajaladherapi yānti pāramāropayanti śivamuttamabodhibījam |
children.translated_text: Having attained which, beings cross even the ocean of birth to the far shore and plant the supreme seed of <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) that leads to <s>Śiva</s> (the auspicious, liberation),

children.text: cintāmaṇerapi samabhyadhikaṃ guṇaughairmānuṣyakaṃ ka iha tadviphalīkaroti || Śl_63 ||
children.translated_text: surpassing even the <s>Cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling gem) in its flood of virtues — who in this world would squander such a human birth? [Śl 63]

children.text: atyantadurlabhamupetya manuṣyabhāvaṃ yadvāñchitaṃ tadabhivāñchitameva kuryāt |
children.translated_text: Having obtained the human state, so exceedingly difficult to attain, one should accomplish whatever is truly to be desired,

children.text: caṇḍānilākulitadīpaśikhācalasya na hyāyuṣaḥ kṣaṇamapi sthitiniścayo'sti || Śl_64 ||
children.translated_text: for there is not even a moment's certainty of the duration of life, which is like the flickering flame of a lamp tossed by a fierce wind. [Śl 64]

children.text: śvaḥ kāryametadidamadya paraṃ muhūrtādetatkṣaṇāditi janena vicintyamāne |
children.translated_text: While people deliberate, 'I shall do this tomorrow, this today, this after just a moment, this in an instant' —

children.text: tiryagnirīkṣaṇapiśaṅgitakāladaṇḍaḥ śaṅke hasatyasahanaḥ kupitaḥ kṛtāntaḥ || Śl_65 ||
children.translated_text: I suspect that <s>Kṛtānta</s> (the God of Death), enraged and impatient, laughs, his staff of death reddened by his sidelong glance. [Śl 65]

children.text: āyāti phullakusumaḥ kusumāgamo 'yameṣā śaśāṅkatilakā śaradāgateti |
children.translated_text: 'This flower-laden spring has come!' — 'Here is autumn, graced by the moon's beauty!' —

children.text: sarvaḥ prahṛṣyati jano na punarmamaitadāyuḥ prahīṇamiti yāti paraṃ viṣādam || Śl_66 ||
children.translated_text: everyone rejoices, yet no one feels the deepest dismay at the thought: 'My life has diminished by this much.' [Śl 66]

children.text: āsannapīnaśaśimaṇḍalamaṇḍanāsu viśrāntavāriguruvāridamekhalāsu |
children.translated_text: Upon the mountain peaks and forest glades, free from attachment, where the full, bright disc of the moon serves as ornament,

children.text: niḥsaṅgamāsu giriśṛṅgavanasthalīṣu dhanyā nayantyanilacañcalaśīlamāyuḥ || Śl_67 ||
children.translated_text: where rain-heavy clouds have ceased to rest and left their watery girdles behind — the blessed ones spend their lives, as fleeting as the wind. [Śl 67]

children.text: kiṃ sā ratirbhavati nandanabhūmikāsu divyāṅganājaghanapṛṣṭhaśilātalāsu |
children.translated_text: Can the pleasure found in the <s>Nandana</s> (divine pleasure-garden) grounds, on stone-slabs smooth as the hips and backs of celestial women,

children.text: yā mugdhamugdhaharaṇīgaṇasevitāsu niḥsaṅgacārusubhagāsu vanasthalīṣu || Śl_68 ||
children.translated_text: compare to that found in the lovely, solitary, and beautiful forest glades frequented by herds of charming, innocent <s>mṛga</s> (deer)? [Śl 68]

children.text: divyāṅganāparimalāvilaye nibhinnasaṃtānakastavakahāsavitaṇvanīṣu |
children.translated_text: Can the pleasure found in the celestial rivers, fragrant with the scent of divine women, where <s>Saṃtānaka</s> blossoms spread their smiling clusters of petals,

children.text: kiṃ sā ratiḥ surasaritsu viviktaramyatīrāsu yā śucijalāsu vane nadīṣu || Śl_69 ||
children.translated_text: compare to that found in the forest streams of pure water, with solitary and delightful banks? [Śl 69]

children.text: viśālāḥ śailānāṃ viratajanasaṃpātasubhagā guhā gāḍhābhogā haritavanalekhāparikarāḥ |
children.translated_text: The vast, deep-recessed caves of the mountains, beautiful in the absence of human crowds, bordered by lines of green forest,

children.text: sarittīrāsannā surajamadhurairnirjanaravairna gamyāḥ kleśāgnerayamiti vadantīva pathikān || Śl_70 ||
children.translated_text: near the riverbanks, with sweet sounds of nature in their solitude — they seem to say to wayfarers: 'This is not the path of the fire of <s>kleśa</s> (afflictions).' [Śl 70]

children.text: māyāmarīcidakacandrataraṃgakalpāḥ kāmā jinena gaditā vibhavāḥ striyaśca |
children.translated_text: Sense-pleasures, riches, and women have been declared by the <s>Jina</s> (the Victorious One, the Buddha) to be like illusions, mirages, water-moons, and waves,

children.text: svapnāntadurlabhitavibhramavipralabdhā bālāḥ patanti nirayeṣvapi yeṣu saktāḥ || Śl_71 ||
children.translated_text: yet the foolish, deceived by the bewildering phantoms found only in dreams, fall even into the hells because of their attachment to these. [Śl 71]

children.text: āpātamātramadhurā viṣayā viṣaśca ghorā viṣākakaṭukā viṣayā viṣaśca |
children.translated_text: Sense-objects and poison are sweet only at first contact; sense-objects and poison are terrible and bitter as the <s>viṣāka</s> plant;

children.text: mohāndhakāragahanā viṣayā viṣaśca durvāravegacapalā viṣayā viṣaśca || Śl_72 ||
children.translated_text: sense-objects and poison are dense with the darkness of delusion; sense-objects and poison are unsteady, driven by an irresistible force. [Śl 72]

children.text: kāmā viṣaśca viṣayāśca nirūpyamānāḥ śreyo viṣaṃ na viṣayā viṣamasvabhāvāḥ |
children.translated_text: When sense-pleasures and poison and sense-objects are carefully examined, poison is preferable to sense-objects, which are treacherous by nature,

children.text: ekatra janmani viṣaṃ viṣatāṃ prayāti janmāntare 'pi viṣayā viṣatāṃ prayānti || Śl_73 ||
children.translated_text: for poison kills only in a single lifetime, whereas sense-objects go on poisoning even in lives to come. [Śl 73]

body.text: viṣasya viṣayāṇāṃ ca dūramatyantagocaram | upayuktaṃ viṣaṃ hanti viṣayāḥ smaraṇādapi || Śl_74 ||
body.translated_text: The difference between poison and sense-objects is vast and extreme: poison kills only when consumed, but sense-objects destroy even by mere recollection. [Śl 74]

children.text: saṃsṛṣṭaṃ vrajati viṣaṃ viṣeṇa śāntiṃ sanmantrairagadadharaiśca sādhyamānam |
children.translated_text: When mixed with other poison, poison is brought to quiescence; treated with proper mantras and those skilled in antidotes, it can be remedied,

children.text: yuktaṃ vā bhavati viṣaṃ hitāya nṝṇāṃ na tvevaṃ viṣayamahāviṣaṃ kadācit || Śl_75 ||
children.translated_text: and poison can even be made beneficial to people when properly applied — but never so the great poison of sense-objects. [Śl 75]

children.text: yadvadvṛṣo viṣamakūpataṭāntatrūḍho dūrvāpravālalavalālasamānasaḥ san |
children.translated_text: Just as a bull clinging to the edge of a treacherous, steep-sided well, his mind fixed greedily on a tuft of fresh <s>dūrvā</s> grass,

children.text: śvabhre patatyatha ca nāstu ta eva lābhastadvatsukhānvitamatiḥ khalu jīvalokaḥ || Śl_76 ||
children.translated_text: falls into the pit, and then that very gain is no more — just so indeed is the world of the living, whose minds are attached to pleasure. [Śl 76]

children.text: mandākinījalarayākulitālakābhiḥ krīḍāvihāramanubhūya sahāpsarobhiḥ |
children.translated_text: Having enjoyed sport and pleasure with <s>Apsaras</s> (celestial nymphs) whose locks are tossed by the spray of the <s>Mandākinī</s> river,

children.text: bhūyo bhramanti kharavaitaraṇe taraṃgasaṃparkajarjaritadāruṇaduḥkhabhājaḥ || Śl_77 ||
children.translated_text: they wander again in the terrible <s>Vaitaraṇī</s> (river of hell), suffering dreadful pain, their bodies torn by its harsh waves. [Śl 77]

children.text: āstīrṇakalpatarupallvasaṃstareṣu kāntāsakhāḥ suravaneṣu makhaṃ vihṛtya |
children.translated_text: Having sported in the celestial groves as companions of beautiful women on beds strewn with <s>Kalpataru</s> (wish-fulfilling tree) blossoms,

children.text: bhūyo bhramanti niśitākulaśastrapātavicchinnagātramasipattravanasthalīṣu || Śl_78 ||
children.translated_text: they wander again in the <s>Asipattravana</s> (sword-leaf forests), their limbs severed by showers of sharp, swarming blade-strokes. [Śl 78]

children.text: sparśe sukhāsu padapātanatonnatāsu merornitambapadavīṣu ciraṃ vihṛtya |
children.translated_text: Having long sported on the slopes of <s>Meru</s>, on terraces that rise and fall softly underfoot, pleasant to the touch,

children.text: uttaptasaikatakukūlakṛśānurāśiṃ saṃsīryamāṇacaraṇorubhujo bhramanti || Śl_79 ||
children.translated_text: they wander again, their feet, thighs, and arms crumbling away upon heaps of scorching sand and burning embers. [Śl 79]

children.text: gatvā divaṃ mukharabhāsurakiṅkanīkahārāvalīnikaradanturitairvimānaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Having gone to heaven, with celestial mansions covered by rows of necklaces of resounding, brilliant little bells,

children.text: ghoraṃ sthirāśrayamameyamanantapāramandhaṃ tamaḥ punaradhaḥśirasā patanti || Śl_80 ||
children.translated_text: they fall headlong again into the terrible, firm-based, immeasurable, boundless, impenetrable darkness. || Śl_80 ||

children.text: śakro 'pi yatra surakiṃnaranāgayakṣamauliprabhāprakarapiñjarapādapīṭhaḥ |
children.translated_text: Where even <s>Śakra</s>, whose footstool is tinged yellow by the luster of the crowns of gods, <s>kiṃnaras</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, and <s>yakṣas</s>,

children.text: karmānilākulagatiḥ kugatiḥ prayāti ko nāma tatra puruṣo na bhayaṃ bhajeta || Śl_81 ||
children.translated_text: proceeds to an evil destiny, his course bewildered by the wind of <s>karma</s> — what man would not take to fear there? || Śl_81 ||

children.text: pramlāyamānakusumāḥ śru x x x digdhā mlānāmbarāḥ karuṇadīkṣitabandhuvargāḥ |
children.translated_text: With wilting flowers, [bodies] smeared..., with faded garments, their kinfolk gazing with pitiful eyes,

children.text: duḥkhaṃ paraṃ yadamarā maraṇe vrajanti tanmānavā na jalabudbudalolajīvāḥ || Śl_82 ||
children.translated_text: if the gods suffer greatly when they face death, what then of humans whose lives are as fleeting as water bubbles? || Śl_82 ||

children.text: duḥkhāgniprakaranirodhabhairave 'sminyaloke vahati janaḥ sukhābhimānam |
children.translated_text: In this terrifying world, where masses of the fire of suffering rage, people carry the notion of happiness;

children.text: tanmatyorvadanamapāvṛtaṃ viśālaṃ tadbījaṃ punarapi janmapādapasya || Śl_83 ||
children.translated_text: that is the wide-open mouth of death, that is the seed of the tree of rebirth. || Śl_83 ||

children.text: taṃ tṛṣṇāmayadṛḍhadīrghatantubaddhaṃ paryastapraṇihitabhīmakāladaṇḍam |
children.translated_text: Bound by the firm, long thread of <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving), with the terrible staff of <s>Kāla</s> (Time) placed upon them,

children.text: sattvānāṃ bhavajaladhau pariplutānāṃ matsyanāṃ baḍiśamivāntakena dattam || Śl_84 ||
children.translated_text: it is like a fishhook given by the Destroyer to beings drowning in the ocean of existence, as to fish. || Śl_84 ||

children.text: kumbhīpākakvathitakalilāduṣṇasaṃrambhavegātkṛtvodgrīvaṃ kṣaṇamapi sukhaṃ labdhaniśvāsamokṣāḥ |
children.translated_text: Lifting their necks for a moment from the boiling liquid of the <s>Kumbhīpāka</s> (hell), gaining a brief respite of breath from the force of the scorching heat,

children.text: krodhāpūrṇaiḥ subahubhirayomudgaraistāḍyamānā manyate taṃ paramiva sukhaṃ nārakā yadvadeva || Śl_85 ||
children.translated_text: being struck by many iron hammers by those filled with rage, the hell-beings consider even that as the highest happiness. || Śl_85 ||

children.text: tadvadduḥkhairaniśamavaśo dāruṇaiḥ pīḍyamānastāvatkālaṃ jaraṇamaṇarakṣobhamuktaḥ kathaṃcit |
children.translated_text: Likewise, being helplessly tormented by terrible sufferings continuously, somehow freed for a time from the agitation of the digestive fires,

children.text: mandībhūte kṣaṇamapi nije duḥsahe duḥkhavahnau sarvo lokastanusukhalavagrāmatṛṣṇāṃ karoti || Śl_86 ||
children.translated_text: when his own unbearable fire of suffering abates for even a moment, every being in the world develops craving for a thin morsel of happiness. || Śl_86 ||

children.text: yāvadyāvajjagati sakale jāyate saukhyasaṃjñā tāvattāvadbahutaraśikho jāyate rāgabahniḥ |
children.translated_text: The more the notion of happiness arises in this entire world, the more the many-flamed fire of passion blazes;

children.text: yāvadyāvadvisarati śubhā bhāvanā bhāvyamānā tāvattāvadbahalataratāmeti mohāndhakāram || Śl_87 ||
children.translated_text: the more the wholesome <s>bhāvanā</s> (meditation) being cultivated fades away, the more the darkness of delusion thickens. || Śl_87 ||

children.text: yāvadyāvanniyatamaśubhā bhāvanā yāti vṛddhim |
children.translated_text: The more the decidedly unwholesome <s>bhāvanā</s> (contemplation) grows,

children.text: tāvattāvattaralataratamiti mohāndhakāram || Śl_88 ||
children.translated_text: the more the darkness of delusion becomes increasingly restless. || Śl_88 ||

children.text: durgandhipūtivikṛtairaravindamindumindīvaraṃ ca tulayanti yadāṅganāṅgaiḥ |
children.translated_text: When they compare the limbs of women — foul-smelling, putrid, and deformed — to lotuses, moons, and blue lotuses,

children.text: tasyānṛtasya phalamugramidaṃ kavīnāṃ tāsveva garbhanilayaṃ padamī viśanti || Śl_89 ||
children.translated_text: this is the terrible fruit of that falsehood of the poets: they enter into the very womb, the abode within those very women. || Śl_89 ||

children.text: kā saugatirjagati yā śataśo na yātā kiṃ tatsukhaṃ yadaśakṛnna purānubhūtam |
children.translated_text: What good destiny in the world has not been traversed hundreds of times? What happiness is that which has not been experienced countless times before?

children.text: kāstāḥ śriyaścapalacāmaracāruhāsāḥ prāptā na yāstadapi vardhata eva rāgaḥ || Śl_90 ||
children.translated_text: What are those glories, with their lovely smiles and waving fly-whisks, that have not been attained? Yet passion still grows. || Śl_90 ||

children.text: nadyo na tā na vihṛtaṃ pulineṣu yāsāṃ sthānaṃ na tajjagati yatra kṛto na vāsaḥ |
children.translated_text: There are no rivers on whose banks one has not sported; there is no place in the world where one has not dwelt;

children.text: vyomnāpi tanna padamasti na yatra yātaṃ duṣpūraṇastadapi vardhata eva rāgaḥ || Śl_91 ||
children.translated_text: not even in the sky is there a spot where one has not gone — yet passion still grows, insatiable. || Śl_91 ||

children.text: duḥkhaṃ na tadyadasakṛnna purānubhūtaṃ kāmā na te jagati yairiha tṛptirāsīt |
children.translated_text: There is no suffering that has not been experienced countless times before; there are no pleasures in the world from which there has been satiation;

children.text: sattvo na so 'sti jaṭhare śayitaṃ na yasya saṃsāriṇastadapi nāsti kathaṃ virāgaḥ || Śl_92 ||
children.translated_text: there is no being in whose belly one has not lain — yet for the one in <s>saṃsāra</s>, how is there no <s>virāga</s> (dispassion)? || Śl_92 ||

children.text: atyāyate jagati janmaparigrahe 'sminduḥkhe sukhe ca bahuśaḥ parivartamānaḥ |
children.translated_text: In this exceedingly long cycle of births, revolving many times through suffering and happiness,

children.text: nāsau jano jagati yo na babhūva bandhurdveṣoragastadapi tiṣṭhati bhīmabhogaḥ || Śl_93 ||
children.translated_text: there is no person in the world who has not been a kinsman; yet the serpent of hatred remains with its terrible coils. || Śl_93 ||

children.text: yaiḥ sārdhametya hasitaṃ lalitaṃ pragītamekatra pītamaśitaṃ ca kṛtāśca goṣṭhyaḥ |
children.translated_text: Those with whom one has met and laughed, played, and sung together, eaten and drunk together in one place, and held gatherings —

children.text: kālakrameṇa gamitāḥ kati ke 'pi ramyā nītāḥ samāśca viṣamāśca daśāḥ kathaṃcit || Śl_94 ||
children.translated_text: through the course of time how many delightful ones have departed, and how many pleasant and unpleasant conditions have been somehow endured! || Śl_94 ||

children.text: tānārjavaṃ javavivartanadṛṣṭanaṣṭānāvartamadhyapatitāniva vīkṣyamāṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: Seeing them — honest ones, appearing and disappearing as they swiftly turn, like those fallen into a whirlpool —

children.text: saṃsārasāgaragatānapahāya bandhūnekaḥ prayāti yadi nāsti tataḥ kṛtaghnaḥ || Śl_95 ||
children.translated_text: if one goes alone, abandoning relatives caught in the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>, then one is ungrateful. || Śl_95 ||

children.text: aṅkasthitena śiśunā vivaśena yāsāṃ pītaḥ payodhararasaṃ praṇayānuyātaḥ |
children.translated_text: The child, helpless, sitting on the lap, drank the milk from those breasts, following with love;

children.text: tanniṣphalapracuradurlalitaikabhājaḥ ko nāma dasyurapi hātumihotsaheta || Śl_96 ||
children.translated_text: who, even a robber, would dare here to abandon those who are the sole recipients of much fruitless tender care? || Śl_96 ||

children.text: yā saṃsthito 'yamudare 'pi kṛtāvakāśo yāḥ snehaviklavadhiyaḥ ślathamenamūhuḥ |
children.translated_text: She in whose womb this one was sheltered, having been given space; those who, with minds unsteady from affection, gently carried him —

children.text: tā duḥkhitā aśaraṇāḥ kṛpaṇā vihāya ko nāma śatrurapi gantumihotsaheta || Śl_97 ||
children.translated_text: who, even an enemy, would dare to go, leaving them suffering, without refuge, pitiable? || Śl_97 ||

children.text: vikīrṇe duḥkhaughairjagati vivaśe 'sminnaśaraṇe parārthe yadduḥkhaṃ tadiha sukhamāhuḥ supuruṣāḥ |
children.translated_text: In this world overwhelmed by floods of suffering, helpless and without refuge, the suffering endured for the sake of others — that, the virtuous declare, is happiness here;

children.text: kṣaṇaṃ kṣuttṛṣṇoṣṇaśramavigamaramyānarucaḥ paraṃ kṛtvā teṣāmapi yadiha ka ivāsya pratisamaḥ || Śl_98 ||
children.translated_text: pleasures delightful only for a moment — the passing of hunger, thirst, heat, and fatigue — without relish; having done the utmost even for those, who indeed is equal to this one? || Śl_98 ||

children.text: na sāramyairyā naiva ca nṛpatilakṣmīparikarairna dārairnāpatyairna surabhavane nāsuragatau |
children.translated_text: Not by pleasures, not by the retinue of royal glory, not by wife, not by offspring, not in the abode of gods, not in the realm of <s>asuras</s> —

children.text: kathaṃcitsaṃprāpyaṃ x viṣayasukhaṃ bhogaparamairlabhante yā prītiṃ parahitasukhādhānaniratāḥ || Śl_99 ||
children.translated_text: the joy that those devoted to bringing benefit and happiness to others obtain, somehow achieved, cannot be matched by those devoted to sensory enjoyment. || Śl_99 ||

children.text: svayaṃ ghāsagrāsaṃ paśurapi karotyeva sulabhaṃ yadṛcchā labdhaṃ vā pibati salilaṃ gāḍhatṛṣitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Even an animal obtains its own easily available fodder and food; a deeply thirsty one drinks whatever water is obtained by chance;

children.text: parasyārtha kartuṃ yadiha puruṣo 'yaṃ prayatate tadasya svaṃ tejaḥ sukhamidamaho pauruṣamidam || Śl_100 ||
children.translated_text: if this person strives here to act for the benefit of another, that is his own splendor, that is happiness — ah, that is true manliness! || Śl_100 ||

children.text: yadālokaṃ kuvan bhramati raviraśrāntaturagaḥ sadālokaṃ dhatte yadagaṇitabhārā vasumatī |
children.translated_text: As the sun with untiring horses wanders creating light for the world, as the earth always bears its immeasurable burden,

children.text: na sa svārthaḥ kaścitprakṛtiriyameva mahatāṃ yadete lokānāṃ hitasukharasaikāntarasikāḥ || Śl_101 ||
children.translated_text: that is not self-interest at all — this is the very nature of the great ones: that they are solely devoted to the taste of benefit and happiness for the world. || Śl_101 ||

children.text: avidyādhūmrāndhabhramaparigatavyākulagatipradīpte duḥkhāgnau patitamavaśaṃ vīkṣya bhuvanam |
children.translated_text: Seeing the world helplessly fallen into the blazing fire of suffering, its course bewildered, wandering blinded by the smoke of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance),

children.text: sphuradvahnijvālā pramathitaśiroveṣṭananibhā yātante ye 'trādbhuta iha puruṣāste sukṛtinaḥ || Śl_102 ||
children.translated_text: those who exert themselves here, as if the blazing flames were unwinding a turban from their own heads — wondrous! — they are the blessed ones. || Śl_102 ||

children.text: avīciṃ gāhante hutavahaśikhāpūritamapi prasarpadromāñcā himanikaracandrāṃśuśiśiram |
children.translated_text: They plunge into <s>Avīci</s> (hell), even though it is filled with tongues of fire, with their hair standing on end as though it were cool with masses of snow and moonbeams;

children.text: parārthe x x x sphuṭanalinahāsāpi nalinī karotyeṣāṃ tāpaṃ hutavahaśikhāsaṃhatiriva || Śl_103 ||
children.translated_text: for the sake of others, even a lotus pond with its blooming lotus-smiles causes them burning like a mass of fire-tongues. || Śl_103 ||

children.text: parahitakaraṇāya baddhakakṣāḥ sukhamasipattravane vasanti santaḥ |
children.translated_text: Having girded themselves for the benefit of others, the saints dwell happily in the <s>Asipattravana</s> (Sword-leaf Forest hell);

children.text: na punaramarasundarīsahāyāḥ kṣaṇamapi nandanakānane ramante || Śl_104 ||
children.translated_text: but they do not delight even for a moment in the <s>Nandana</s> grove accompanied by celestial nymphs. || Śl_104 ||

children.text: aśaraṇajanatāraṇāya tīrṇāḥ punarapi vaitaraṇīṃ taranti dhīrāḥ |
children.translated_text: Having crossed over for the sake of saving the helpless, the steadfast ones cross the <s>Vaitaraṇī</s> (river of hell) again;

children.text: na tu gaganasarittaraṃgabhaṅgavyatikarasaṅgasukhaṃ svayaṃ bhajante || Śl_105 ||
children.translated_text: but they do not themselves enjoy the pleasure of mingling with the breaking waves of the celestial river. || Śl_105 ||

children.text: iti sucaritaratnaṃ bhūṣaṇaṃ bhūṣaṇānāṃ śivamamṛtamudāraṃ bhāsuraṃ bhāsurāṇām |
children.translated_text: Thus, good conduct is a jewel, an ornament among ornaments, auspicious, immortal, noble, brilliant among the brilliant,

children.text: asulabhamakṛtajñairnandanaṃ nandanānāṃ bhaja samasukhahetuṃ maṅgalaṃ maṅgalānām || Śl_106 ||
children.translated_text: unattainable by the ungrateful, a delight of delights — embrace it as the cause of universal happiness, the most auspicious of all auspicious things! || Śl_106 ||

children.text: sugatavacanapuṣpaṃ sarvadā sevanīyaṃ phalati phalamudāraṃ puṣpameva drumāṇām |
children.translated_text: The flower of the <s>Sugata</s>'s words should always be cultivated, for indeed the flower of trees bears noble fruit;

children.text: sugatavacanapuṣpādartharāśirniṣevyo madhuni mudhakarāṇāṃ yasya vāñchāprakarṣam || Śl_107 ||
children.translated_text: from the flower of the <s>Sugata</s>'s words, the treasure of meaning should be gathered, like honey by bees, in which desire reaches its peak. || Śl_107 ||

children.text: visṛja viṣayānnītyākīrṇāṃ kṣaṇavyayasaṅgino bhaja samasukhaṃ sākāṅkṣaṃ kṛtāntabhayojjhitam |
children.translated_text: Abandon sense-pleasures, strewn with deception, that perish in a moment; embrace universal happiness, eagerly sought, free from the fear of death;

children.text: vikara timiraṃ mohavyājaṃ vimokṣayathārgalaṃ na khalu suciraṃ nidrāyante sadaśvakiśorakāḥ || Śl_108 ||
children.translated_text: dispel the darkness that is the pretext of delusion, unlock the bolt of <s>vimokṣa</s> (liberation) — for excellent young horses do not sleep for long! || Śl_108 ||

children.text: vinayavisaro vīryaskandhaḥ kṣamādamapallavaḥ śamathakusumaḥ prajñāśākhaḥ pradānaghanacchadaḥ |
children.translated_text: With the trunk of <s>vinaya</s> (discipline), the boughs of <s>vīrya</s> (vigor), the shoots of <s>kṣamā</s> (patience) and <s>dama</s> (self-control), the flowers of <s>śamatha</s> (tranquility), the branches of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), the dense foliage of <s>pradāna</s> (generosity),

children.text: praṇidhiśikharaḥ śīlacchāyaḥ praśāntiphalaprado bhava bhava marau tāpārtānāṃ tvamekamahādrumaḥ || Śl_109 ||
children.translated_text: the peak of <s>praṇidhi</s> (aspiration), the shade of <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct), bearing the fruit of <s>praśānti</s> (peace) — become, become in the desert the one great tree for those tormented by heat! || Śl_109 ||

children.text: bahujanahito mābhairvādapradānamahāsvanaḥ pṛthutaraśodhārāsāraḥ kṛpānilacoditaḥ |
children.translated_text: Benefiting many, fearless, with the great thunder of discourse and giving, with extensive heavy showers, driven by the wind of <s>kṛpā</s> (compassion),

children.text: praśamitarajaḥ śīlacchāyāvibhūṣitabhūtalo bhava bhava marau tāpārtānāṃ tvamekamahāghanaḥ || Śl_110 ||
children.translated_text: with dust settled, the ground adorned with the shade of <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct) — become, become in the desert the one great cloud for those tormented by heat! || Śl_110 ||

children.text: prakaṭavipulaṃ paṅkāgādhaḥ prasannatarāśrayaḥ satataśiśiro jālavyālapramādavivarjitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Widely open and vast, with depths free of mud, with the clearest foundation, perpetually cool, free from the danger of nets, traps, and heedlessness,

children.text: prakṛtisubhagastṛṣṇācchedāvimardabharakṣamo bhava bhava marau tāpārtānāṃ tvamekamahāhradaḥ || Śl_111 ||
children.translated_text: beautiful by nature, capable of bearing the pressure of cutting and crushing <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (thirst/craving) — become, become in the desert the one great lake for those tormented by heat! || Śl_111 ||

children.text: iti nigadatā yadupārjitaṃ puṇyaṃ mayā kiyatsugatacarite kṛtvā śraddhāmanena jano 'khilaḥ |
children.translated_text: Whatever merit has been earned by me, speaking thus, having placed faith in the conduct of the <s>Sugata</s>, however little,

children.text: satatasukhito ramyābhogaḥ samṛddhamanorathaḥ parahitarataḥ sarvajñatvaṃ prayātu tataḥ śanaiḥ || Śl_112 ||
children.translated_text: may all people, always happy, with delightful enjoyments, with fulfilled desires, devoted to the benefit of others, gradually proceed to <s>sarvajñatva</s> (omniscience). || Śl_112 ||

children.text: karatalasamāḥ spaṣṭālokāḥ praśāntakṛśānavaḥ sthalakamalinīpattracchannā bisāṅkuradanturāḥ |
children.translated_text: Level as the palm of the hand, with clear light, with fires extinguished, covered with lotus leaves, studded with lotus root sprouts,

children.text: śucisurabhayaḥ sphullāmbhojairvibhūṣitabhūmayo dadhatu narakāḥ sphītāṃ śobhāṃ saśīkaravāyavaḥ || Śl_113 ||
children.translated_text: pure and fragrant, with grounds adorned by blooming lotuses — may the hells attain abundant beauty, with breezes bearing moonbeams! || Śl_113 ||

children.text: vijitaṃvirutamārānīkāḥ kṛtābhayaghoṣaṇā gaganasalilakrīḍā ramyā sameta narāmarāḥ |
children.translated_text: Having conquered and routed the armies of <s>Māra</s>, having proclaimed fearlessness, with delightful sports in celestial waters, may humans and gods come together!

children.text: jananamaraṇakleśāyāsaprabandhavighātino diśi diśi sadā buddhotpādā bhavantu samīhitāḥ || Śl_114 ||
children.translated_text: May the arising of <s>Buddhas</s>, which destroys the continuous succession of the afflictions of birth and death, always occur in every direction as desired! (Verse 114)

children.text: bhavatu jagatāṃ dharmāmodaḥ prabandhamahotsavaḥ suciraguṇitā mṛtyorbandhyā bhavantu manorathāḥ |
children.translated_text: May the fragrance of <s>Dharma</s> become a continuous great festival for all beings! May the wishes of <s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death) be rendered barren for a long time!

children.text: munijanakathāgoṣṭhībandhaiḥ samāvṛtavarṣibhiḥ satataśiśiraḥ subhagacandrālokaḥ prayātu kṛtārthatām || Śl_115 ||
children.translated_text: May the beautiful moonlight, ever cool, accompanied by assemblies engaged in conversations about the words of the sages, attain its purpose! (Verse 115)

body.translated_text: Thus concludes the <s>Dharma</s>-poem (<s>dharmakāvya</s>) called the Letter to a Disciple (<s>Śiṣyalekha</s>).
